title: Why Ground Coffee Prices Are Surging to Record Highs

segments.label: scene 1 (title)
segments.text: Your morning brew has never cost this much. In April 2026, ground coffee hit an unprecedented record high of $9.72 per pound across the United States.

segments.label: scene 2 (statement)
segments.text: That sudden spike left millions of coffee drinkers facing serious sticker shock at the grocery checkout.

segments.label: scene 3 (compare)
segments.text: Relief has been minimal. By September 2026, the average price edged down slightly to $9.33 per pound.

segments.label: scene 4 (gauge)
segments.text: That represents a drop of just 4% from the peak, keeping prices near historic highs.

segments.label: scene 5 (line)
segments.text: Look back to January 2000, when a pound of ground coffee cost a modest $3.54.

segments.label: scene 6 (multiline)
segments.text: By September 2026, the price was 2.6 times that level, marking a total surge of 164%.

segments.label: scene 7 (statement)
segments.text: Over that same span, overall consumer prices increased by 99%. Why has coffee detached so radically from normal inflation?

segments.label: scene 8 (line)
segments.text: To understand today's record highs, we have to look back to the early 2000s. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, ground coffee hit a low of $2.75 per pound in June 2004.

segments.label: scene 9 (counter)
segments.text: By January 2005, prices started creeping back up, reaching $3.05 per pound.

segments.label: scene 10 (multiline)
segments.text: From January 2005 to September 2026, coffee prices surged 206%. By comparison, overall consumer prices rose 76%.

segments.label: scene 11 (statement)
segments.text: Ground coffee was no longer staying cheap. Expanding demand and shifting weather began straining global supply.

segments.label: scene 12 (compare)
segments.text: By January 2010, ground coffee was averaging $3.81 per pound.

segments.label: scene 13 (bars)
segments.text: Since January 2010, coffee climbed 145%, while overall inflation increased 55%.

segments.label: scene 14 (line)
segments.text: Coffee was establishing a much higher baseline price floor. That fundamental shift set the stage for even bigger shocks later.

segments.label: scene 15 (multiline)
segments.text: By January 2015, ground coffee averaged $4.74 per pound. Since January 2015, coffee climbed 97%, while overall inflation rose 43%.

segments.label: scene 16 (counter)
segments.text: Then came 2020. In January 2020, ground coffee stood at $4.17 a pound before unprecedented disruptions hit global supply.

segments.label: scene 17 (bars)
segments.text: From January 2020 to September 2026, ground coffee surged 124%. Overall consumer prices rose 30% across that same timeframe.

segments.label: scene 18 (line)
segments.text: Severe weather and shipping bottlenecks triggered rapid retail spikes. By December 2022, coffee reached $6.46 per pound, climbing 30% in a single year.

segments.label: scene 19 (statement)
segments.text: That pressure only intensified. By January 2025, ground coffee jumped to $7.02 per pound as supply constraints compounded.

segments.label: scene 20 (compare)
segments.text: Between January 2025 and September 2026, coffee prices gained another 33%. General inflation grew just 5% over those months.

segments.label: scene 21 (heatmap)
segments.text: Over the last year, ground coffee rose 2.1%, while broader consumer prices grew 3.7%. Retail prices remain significantly elevated.

segments.label: scene 22 (statement)
segments.text: Retail coffee prices do not surge in a vacuum. Behind these soaring bills lies a perfect storm of climate events and supply chain vulnerabilities.

segments.label: scene 23 (line)
segments.text: Inflation was already building across the economy. By June 2022, overall consumer prices spiked 9% over the preceding year, raising processing and transportation costs.

segments.label: scene 24 (statement)
segments.text: On top of inflation, severe weather hit key farming regions. Freak frosts and historic droughts devastated crops across South America, crippling harvests.

segments.label: scene 25 (heatmap)
segments.text: Monthly price swings reflected these crop losses. Sudden freezes in Brazil drastically reduced yield potential across entire harvest cycles.

segments.label: scene 26 (statement)
segments.text: Shipping chaos compounded agricultural losses. Container shortages and maritime bottlenecks delayed green coffee deliveries, driving ocean freight rates to record levels.

segments.label: scene 27 (compare)
segments.text: When extreme weather coincided with freight bottlenecks, coffee prices surged far faster than general inflation. Supply shocks quickly overwhelmed standard market buffers.

segments.label: scene 28 (gauge)
segments.text: Together, climate shocks and shipping bottlenecks pushed coffee into historically high territory. The supply chain remains deeply vulnerable to future extreme events.

segments.label: scene 29 (statement)
segments.text: Why does a bag of coffee feel so much heavier on the wallet? The answer lies in how far coffee prices have detached from the rest of the grocery aisle.

segments.label: scene 30 (bars)
segments.text: Since January 2000, ground coffee prices have climbed 164%. That is significantly higher than the 99% increase seen in the broader consumer price index.

segments.label: scene 31 (line)
segments.text: Coffee is not just following the inflation trend; it is accelerating away from it. By September 2026, the price was 2.6 times what it was in January 2000.

segments.label: scene 32 (bars)
segments.text: Look at the price history since 2005. Ground coffee surged 206% in that window, while general consumer goods rose 76%.

segments.label: scene 33 (line)
segments.text: This isn't just a minor fluctuation; it shows coffee is increasingly vulnerable to volatile supply chains and climate shocks.

segments.label: scene 34 (kpi)
segments.text: Even in the last year, while overall inflation hit 3.7%, the premium paid for your morning brew remains stubbornly high at $9.33 per pound.

segments.label: scene 35 (line)
segments.text: The price floor for coffee has fundamentally shifted. We are paying more because the global supply system has struggled to keep pace with demand.

segments.label: scene 36 (statement)
segments.text: Agricultural vulnerability is now a permanent feature of your grocery bill. Coffee is a bellwether for how climate shifts disrupt global trade.

segments.label: scene 37 (bars)
segments.text: Since 2010, ground coffee has surged 145%. General inflation climbed only 55% in that same period.

segments.label: scene 38 (line)
segments.text: In April 2026, prices peaked at $9.72 per pound. While they have since dipped by 4%, the trend remains alarmingly elevated.

segments.label: scene 39 (kpi)
segments.text: While broader inflation has been relatively flat at 0% change from the recent high, coffee remains costly. The supply chain has not yet fully recovered.

segments.label: scene 40 (multiline)
segments.text: We are seeing a systemic shift where agricultural goods outpace the cost of other living expenses. Your morning cup reflects these deep structural changes.
